video_caption: The video begins with a man, likely in his 50s or 60s, with dark hair, black-framed glasses, a black suit jacket, and a white shirt, speaking to the camera and occasionally gesturing with his right hand. He is seated in what appears to be an empty auditorium, with rows of unoccupied red chairs visible in the background. On the right side of the screen, the title "THE SMART WEAPON AI" is displayed in dark blue text. A quick transition then shows a white circular logo with a white 'S' inside, initially against a blurred gradient background that shifts from light blue/grey to red/orange. This quickly changes to a solid grey-white background, and the logo is updated with red and blue arcs within the 'S' circle, followed by the text "STIFTERVERBAND" and "Bildung. Wissenschaft. Innovation." (Education. Science. Innovation.) below it. The scene cuts back to the man, who continues to speak and gesture, now looking slightly off-camera to his left. Text appears on the right side of the screen, identifying him as "Neil Jacobstein, Chair of the Artificial Intelligence & Robotics Track, Singularity University, Mountain View California," which then fades away. The video concludes with the text "Jede Woche neue Videos!" (New videos every week!) appearing at the bottom of the screen against a red background.

The video opens with a man, appearing to be in his 50s or 60s, with dark, slicked-back hair and glasses, wearing a white collared shirt and a black suit jacket. He is seated and speaking directly to the camera, gesturing occasionally with his right hand. Behind him are numerous rows of empty red chairs, set in what looks like an auditorium or conference hall with light-colored walls. At 0:12, the scene transitions to a white screen displaying a logo featuring a stylized 'S' within a circle, colored red, gray, and blue. Below the logo, the question "Innovation or regulation?" appears in black text. The video then cuts back to a closer shot of the same man, who continues to speak thoughtfully, maintaining eye contact with the camera, with the red chairs now blurred in the background.

The video opens with a medium shot of a man with dark, slicked-back hair and glasses, wearing a black suit jacket over a white shirt, speaking directly to the camera with a serious expression against a blurred background of red seats. At the 0:09 mark, a white panel slides in from the right, revealing text: "NEIL JACOBSTEIN" in large, bold letters, followed by "He served in a variety of executive and technical advisory roles for industry, nonprofit, and government organizations." The man continues speaking as the text is displayed, his mouth moving as he articulates. The text panel then slides out at 0:18, returning to the man speaking. At 0:29, the scene abruptly cuts to a plain white screen. A small circular logo, featuring a stylized red and blue 'S', appears at the top center, and below it, the question "Should we ban smart weapons?" is displayed in dark blue text, signifying the topic of discussion.

The video opens with a close-up shot of a man with dark, slicked-back hair and glasses, wearing a black suit jacket over a white collared shirt. He is speaking directly to the camera, his mouth moving as he articulates his thoughts, with a slightly engaged and serious expression. The background is softly blurred, showing rows of red auditorium seats. At 00:34, the scene transitions to a white screen featuring a dark teal, left-pointing arrow graphic. Inside this arrow, white text reads: "Jede Woche neu beim Stifterverband: Die Zukunftsmacher und ihre Visionen für Bildung, Wissenschaft und Innovation." (English: "New every week at Stifterverband: The Future Makers and their Visions for Education, Science and Innovation."). Below this, smaller red text states: "ABONNIEREN SIE DEN YOUTUBE-CHANNEL DES STIFTERVERBANDES" (English: "SUBSCRIBE TO THE YOUTUBE CHANNEL OF THE STIFTERVERBAND"). In the bottom left corner, additional credits appear in black text: "Autorin: Corina Niebuhr | Produktion: Webclip Medien Berlin Redaktion: Michael Sonnabend, Nadine Bührung, Björn Quick | Videodesign: KreativeKK.de" (English: "Author: Corina Niebuhr | Production: Webclip Medien Berlin Editorial Staff: Michael Sonnabend, Nadine Bührung, Björn Quick | Video Design: KreativeKK.de"). This end screen functions as a promotional message for the Stifterverband's YouTube channel.
